nodes.label: Dorsi delle carte (card backs)
nodes.rationale: Six full-image 5:7 backs (Il Grande Rosone, Codice Arcano, Eclisse, Trama di Radici, Cuore della Fornace, Occhio degli Abissi) — one neutral plus one per faction theme, so a deck back can echo its Casata.

nodes.label: Site batch 4: Casata banners (3:2)
nodes.rationale: One 3:2 image per faction, reused across Cronache, deck screens and filters instead of a separate asset per surface.

nodes.label: Legendary entrance reveal
nodes.rationale: Each of the 16 legendaries gets faction-coloured rays, a name card and its own sound motif (LEGEND_VOICE in audio/sfx.ts); rays vanish under Reduce animations.

nodes.label: Revealed hand (HandCard.known)
nodes.rationale: Occhio Vacuo flips cards to known and they stay face-up at the top of the table until played, with an eye marker on your own cards the opponent has seen — information is made persistent and symmetric instead of a one-off peek.

nodes.label: Signori di Casata (tribal lords)
nodes.rationale: One lord per faction grants a faction-shaped buff (Brace +1 attack, Marea +1 health, Radice Linfa vitale, Vuoto Eco) so the tribal archetype has an anchor.

nodes.label: Full-art vertical 5:7 format
nodes.rationale: Recommended format because it matches the game's Illustrata style; the subject is pushed into the upper two thirds and the lower third kept dark, calm and low-detail so rules text can be laid over the art.

nodes.label: Horizontal 4:3 classic frame format
nodes.rationale: Alternative classic inset illustration: single centred subject, readable at small size — no text-safe zone needed because the frame keeps text outside the art.

nodes.label: 60 missing card illustrations
nodes.rationale: Backlog file for the 60 cards added when the set grew to 120; each entry also records the card's type and Casata (e.g. 'Unita, Brace') so the prompt's setting clause can be picked correctly.

nodes.label: 12 new card illustrations
nodes.rationale: Art for the 12 cards added to fill the missing archetypes (tribal, ramp, tutor, prison, sweeper, evasion) when the set went from 60 to 72; three per Casata.

nodes.label: AI art pipeline (npm run art)
nodes.rationale: Prompts live in art/prompts.json as common style + subject + faction setting, with no artist names, text or logos; images land in src/assets/art/<id>.png and are picked up by import.meta.glob so adding art needs no code change. Provider-swappable (OpenAI or Stability).

nodes.label: d3-delaunay glass tessellation
nodes.rationale: Used to generate the glass tiles of the Vetrata (stained glass) card style procedurally.

nodes.label: game-icons.net CC BY 3.0 attribution
nodes.rationale: Procedural figures use game-icons.net icons (Lorc, Delapouite and others) under CC BY 3.0; attribution lives in the Collection screen and the mapping in art/icon-map.json regenerated via npm run icons.

nodes.label: Set Base (120 cards)
nodes.rationale: Grew 60 -> 72 -> 120 cards (44 common, 32 uncommon, 28 rare, 16 legendary), 30 per Casata, balanced with AI simulations keeping factions between 48% and 53% win rate at every deck level.

nodes.label: Card styles (Dipinta, Vetrata, Incisione, Illustrata)
nodes.rationale: All styles moved to a single full-art model with a title bar and an attack/health plate; Illustrata is free but only offered when the AI image exists, otherwise cards fall back to Vetrata.

nodes.label: Common art style directive
nodes.rationale: Every prompt repeats the same opening clause (painterly dark-fantasy oil painting, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich jewel tones, subtle stained-glass light rays, gothic cathedral mood, visible brushstrokes) and the same negative tail (no text, letters, numbers, logo, watermark, signature, frame, border, card template, UI) so independently generated images stay a coherent set and never bake in card chrome the UI already draws.

nodes.label: Legal note on AI-generated images
nodes.rationale: In many jurisdictions (e.g. the USA) fully AI-generated images are not covered by copyright, so others could reuse them; provider terms must also be checked. This is the stated risk of the AI art pipeline.

nodes.label: Rintocco (trigger when your Seal breaks)

nodes.rationale: Turns losing a Seal into a comeback resource, so the board state that ends the game also fuels resistance.

nodes.label: Sigilli (three lanes, three seals per side)

nodes.label: Sincronie (14 lore-linked card pairs)
nodes.rationale: Pairs bound by the lore (Lupa Grigia + Orsa Madre, Il Primo Fuoco + Fenice Minore) reward flavour-coherent deckbuilding; implemented in engine/mechanics.ts.

nodes.label: index.html app shell
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite entry: lang="it", a single #root div and a module script pointing at /src/main.tsx; everything else is rendered by React.

nodes.label: Image-to-video looping animation prompts
nodes.rationale: Feed the finished full-art image back into an image-to-video model: 4 second seamless loop, static camera, subject keeps its exact shape and pose with only a slow breathing motion, so the animated card stays recognisably the same card.

nodes.label: Google Fonts preconnect and font set
nodes.norm_label: google fonts preconnect and font set
nodes.rationale: Loads Grenze Gotisch, Alegreya Sans, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Cinzel and EB Garamond — exactly the Gotico / Leggibile / Elegante accessibility font choices, with Atkinson Hyperlegible as the readable option.

nodes.label: Options and accessibility
nodes.rationale: Text size, reduced motion, high contrast, three font choices (Gotico, Leggibile, Elegante) and volume; every animation honours the reduced-motion preference.

nodes.label: npm run build:single (single-file dist/index.html)
nodes.rationale: Bundles the whole game into one HTML file openable by double click, for demos and previews, alongside the classic static build.

nodes.label: Inline data-URI SVG rose-window favicon
nodes.rationale: Favicon and apple-touch-icon are base64 SVG data URIs (an eight-petal rose window in gold and crimson) rather than files, so the single-file build:single output stays genuinely self-contained with no external requests.

nodes.label: engine/ pure rules engine
nodes.rationale: Rules, effects and AI kept free of React so the engine is portable to a server (and it was in fact ported to C# for rosarcana-unity).

nodes.label: Mulligan
nodes.rationale: One-shot replacement before the first turn; the AI heuristic replaces cards costing 5 or more.

nodes.label: Replay system
nodes.rationale: Every match is recorded move by move so it can be replayed from the end screen or the Profile with a scrub bar.

nodes.label: Turn clock (TURN_SECONDS / RESERVE_SECONDS)
nodes.rationale: 75s per turn plus a 60s match-long reserve; animations do not consume time and teaching modes are untimed, so the clock never punishes learning or slow rendering.

nodes.label: rosarcana-unity C# engine port
nodes.rationale: The pure engine was ported to C# in a separate project, which is only feasible because engine/ has no React dependency.

nodes.label: Zustand stores (profile + battle)
nodes.rationale: Split into profile/store.ts (collection, currencies, decks, persisted in the browser) and features/battle/store.ts (match state plus the animation director).

nodes.label: Framer Motion animation layer
nodes.rationale: MTG Arena style animations without hand-written animation code; AnimatePresence for exits and spring attacks.

nodes.label: Stable layoutId card-<id>
nodes.rationale: Each card keeps a stable layoutId so the same card element flies hand -> stack -> lane automatically; avoids writing manual animation code for every transition.
